A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELECTRAFI study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original charge-density prediction, inference-time and DFT initialization experiments, with element-wise analyses and density examples in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds rotation-augmentation results, distributional and spectral analyses, and frequencies of individual DFT slowdowns.

M1.justification: The Gaussian parameterization, EScAIP backbone, dyadic readout, Fourier/Poisson construction, inverse FFT and electron-count normalization are retained. Appendix B is unchanged. Rotation augmentation is investigated as an additional experimental condition; the proposed core algorithm remains the same.

E1.justification: MP-Full, GNoME, ECD-HSE06, MP-Mixed and Cubic remain the benchmark datasets. V2 adds evaluation on randomly rotated ECD-HSE06 structures, extending coverage beyond the original fixed coordinate frame.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain ChargE3Net, DeepDFT, SCDP, GPWNO and InfGCN with the same participation in Table 1. The DFT comparisons retain SAD, converged-density initialization and ChargE3Net. Newly cited atomistic models are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported maximum-neighbor setting changes from 300 to 200 for MP-Mixed and MP-Full (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 7), without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Appendix C adds controlled combinations of rotated and unrotated training/testing. Dataset splits, hardware and the non-magnetic DFT filtering protocol are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix C tests rotation sensitivity and augmentation; Appendix F.2–F.3 adds composition-distribution and reciprocal-space error analyses; Section 4.1 quantifies individual structures with negative time savings. The earlier element-wise analysis and density case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added rotation table and spectral plots continue reporting point estimates or mean curves without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds rotation-test NMAEs of 1.69% without augmentation and 1.33% with augmentation, individual slowdown frequencies, and composition/spectral findings. Table 1 revises ELECTRAFI timings from 0.24 to 0.17 seconds for MP-Full/MP-Mixed and from 0.15 to 0.11 seconds for GNoME; corresponding speedups become 463× and 302×. Table 2 slightly revises total-time savings. Existing benchmark NMAEs and SCF counts remain unchanged. The neighbor-setting revision prevents treating the timing differences as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equation (16) changes the NMAE integration domain from all of R3 to the periodic simulation cell, correcting the formal definition for periodic densities. The core Fourier/Poisson derivation and Appendix B mathematics remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same claims: analytic periodization of local Gaussians, competitive accuracy, up to 633× faster inference and approximately 20% end-to-end DFT savings. Reworded contribution bullets and new supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive applicability qualifications concerning fixed-frame versus rotated inputs, individual DFT slowdowns and requirements for magnetic materials. It expands explanations of the MP–GNoME generalization gap using composition, cell size and spectral content, and explains the resolution-dependent difficulty of directly predicting Fourier coefficients.

D1.justification: The Software and Data statement replaces a future-release promise with reported public code availability, a repository address and a license reference. V2 newly specifies full-grid loss evaluation without subsampling and revises the MP neighbor limits. The detailed VASP setup and hardware disclosures were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Qu et al. (2026), Mazitov et al. (2025) and Kresse and Joubert (1999), and sharpens its discussion of GPWNO and learned rotation robustness. Several other bibliography changes update publication metadata for existing works rather than adding research.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the introduction to explain SCF initialization more clearly, moves the training-objective description into Methods, adds discussion subheadings and a notation guide, and inserts the new appendix material. Publication, affiliation and disclosure text also changes, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands visual explanation with an end-to-end workflow diagram, composition and spectral plots, and notation and rotation-result tables. Figure 1 is resized and relocated, and the DFT-savings caption is expanded. Existing element heatmaps and density examples are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 provides better support and clearer limits through the rotation study, distributional analyses and explicit individual slowdown rates, addressing gaps in v1's aggregate evaluations. The workflow diagram, full-grid disclosure and code-access information also improve usability. These gains are bounded: core accuracy results remain unchanged, uncertainty reporting is still absent, and the relationship between revised neighbor limits and lower timings is unexplained.
